One thing that may help:

Decades ago, Judith Martin, aka Miss Manners, got a question about pagers going off in movie theaters. It was her observation that with every new technology, some people thought manners no longer applied.

But eventually people come around. I saw this happen with both dumbphones and smartphones in theaters. The great bulk of people learned not to be jackasses.

It's a very human thing. Once babies find their voices, they use them. Gradually they learn to use them more subtly. When we gain a new power, we test its limits and learn to develop finer control as we see the impacts.

It's already happening with "AI". I just watched an episode of a show where somebody had to write wedding vows. Her friend walked away saying, "And don't use AI. I'll know."

Things will change, of course. But much will be preserved.
